els.text: eavesdropper · reads everything on the wire
✕ 5ˣ mod 23 = 8 → x = ? · infeasible at real sizes

note: Everything starts in the open. g = 5 and p = 23 are public constants; the eavesdropper holds them too.
Each side picks a private number and keeps it, a = 6 in the browser, b = 15 in the server. These two numbers never touch the wire.
The browser computes its share A = 5⁶ mod 23 = 8 and sends it. The eavesdropper records it.
The server computes B = 5¹⁵ mod 23 = 19 and sends it back, recorded too. The wire has now carried everything it will ever carry: 5, 23, 8, and 19.
Each side raises the share it received to its own private number, 19⁶ mod 23 = 2 in the browser, 8¹⁵ mod 23 = 2 in the server. Both equal 5⁹⁰ mod 23, the same number, never sent.

The eavesdropper holds 5, 23, 8, and 19, and needs a or b to go further: which power of 5 gives 8, mod 23? Trial finds it instantly at this size; with p hundreds of digits long, no known method finishes. The shares alone are worthless.
